straight_course.bias_notes: Straight course hosting 5f, 6f, 7f, and straight 1m races. Features a continuous uphill grade. On Good to Firm ground, high draws (stands side rail) often hold a distinct advantage ('Golden Highway'). On Soft to Heavy ground, low draws (far side rail) become highly competitive. Pace positioning is critical—runners drawn adjacent to the primary early speed receive a crucial 'tow' before the stiff final furlong.
straight_course.post_bias: In large-field handicaps (e.g., Wokingham, Royal Hunt Cup), high draws (stands side) are generally favored on fast ground. However, following the pace tow is more important than raw stall numbers. Avoid middle draws if the field splits into two isolated groups.

round_course.bias_notes: Right-handed, triangular circuit. Sweeps downhill into Swinley Bottom before beginning a grueling 73-foot uphill climb to the winning post. Despite the stiff hill, the final straight run-in is only 2.5 furlongs (500m); horses entering the straight on or near the lead ('E' / 'P') can slingshot off the final bend and prove exceptionally hard to run down.
round_course.post_bias: In 1m2f and 1m4f round course races, low barriers (1-5) offer a modest advantage by allowing runners to save ground entering Swinley Bottom. High draws in large fields risk getting hung wide on the sweeping turns.

handicapping_angles.stiff_73ft_uphill_finish: The 73-foot elevation climb from Swinley Bottom to the post acts as a severe stamina filter. One-dimensional speed horses without proven distance stamina hit a wall in the final 100 yards. Aggressively upgrade horses with strong L2f (last 2 furlongs) closing sectionals.
handicapping_angles.straight_course_pace_tow: On the straight course (5f to 1m), identify where the early speed is drawn. Runners drawn within 2-3 stalls of the lead pace-setters benefit from cover and a drag-effect before launching their effort inside the 2f pole.
handicapping_angles.round_course_prominent_slingshot: Do not assume Ascot's round course always favors deep closers. Tactical pressers ('P') who turn for home in the top 3 with clear running room regularly hold off swoopers due to the short 500m straight run-in.
handicapping_angles.royal_ascot_class_spike: During Royal Ascot (June) and British Champions Day (October), local British handicap form is heavily tested by elite Group 1 international shippers (Ireland, France, USA, Australia). Heavily upgrade Tier 1 international pattern form over domestic handicappers.
handicapping_angles.uk_handicap_weight_impact: In British Official Rating (OR) Handicaps (Class 2 to Class 4), weight is critical—every 2 lbs (1kg) equals approximately 1 length over Ascot's stiff uphill straight. In Group / Weight-For-Age (WFA) feature events (Gold Cup, King George, Prince of Wales's), ignore weight spreads and prioritize peak Class and Racing Post Ratings (RPR).
